349419.title: Uniform-mass conjecture for cycles
349419.statement:
Let $C_m$ be the cycle on $m$ edges, let $E(C_m)$ be its edge set, and let $\beta(C_m,1)$ be the optimization parameter defined in the paper. **Uniform-mass conjecture for cycles.** For all $m\geq 3$, $\beta(C_m,1)$ is achieved by the uniform distribution on $E(C_m)$. In particular,

$$
\beta(C_m,1)=m^{-m}.
$$

The paper explains that this is open in general; it considers the cases $m=5,6$ approachable, while its methods do not settle $m=7$.

355385.title: Conjecture that the two layered-number sequences coincide
355385.statement:
For each positive integer $i$, let $g_i$ and $k_i$ denote the two integer sequences defined in the paper, where $g_i$ is the least integer admitting an $i$-layered partition and $k_i$ is the least $i$-layered number. **Sequence-equality conjecture.**

$$
g_i=k_i
$$

for every positive integer $i$. The conjecture asserts that the least integer with an $i$-layered partition is itself the least $i$-layered number; the supplied context gives examples for $i=5,6,7,8$.

355934.title: Saxton's permanent submatrix conjecture
355934.statement:
Let $B\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ be a matrix. For each $j\in[m]$, let the support of its $j$th column be $\{i\in[n]:B_{ij}\neq 0\}$. **Saxton's conjecture.** If, for every $J\subset[m]$,

$$
\left|\bigcup_{j\in J}\{i\in[n]:B_{ij}\neq 0\}\right|\geq 2|J|-1,
$$

then $B$ contains an $m\times m$ submatrix with non-zero permanent. If true, this would imply that every essential cover of the $n$-cube has at least $\lceil n/2\rceil+1$ hyperplanes, matching the best-known constructions; the supplied source does not establish whether the conjecture is resolved.

356173.title: Pointwise kernel domination conjecture for probabilistic discrete Riesz transforms
356173.statement:
For $d\geq2$, let $K_{\mathbb{H}^{(k)}}$ and $K_{R_\mathrm{dis}^{(k)}}$ be the kernels of the probabilistic and Calderón–Zygmund discrete Riesz transforms, respectively, with $n\in\mathbb{Z}^d$ and $k=1,\dots,d$. **Pointwise kernel domination conjecture.** For every $n\in\mathbb{Z}^d$,

$$
\left|K_{\mathbb{H}^{(k)}}(n)\right|\geq\left|K_{R_\mathrm{dis}^{(k)}}(n)\right|.
$$

The comparison is supported by numerical simulations and is known when $d=1$; the conjecture concerns all dimensions $d\geq2$.

356347.title: Golowich's conjecture on regularity of large homogeneous equations
356347.statement:
Let a linear homogeneous equation have nonzero integer coefficients, not all of the same sign. **Golowich's conjecture.** For each positive integer $k$ there is an integer $m(k)$ such that for any $m\ge m(k)$, any such equation in $m$ variables is $k$-regular.

This conjecture predicts that sufficiently many variables force bounded color-regularity for every fixed number of colors. The source states that it is false, so the proposed uniform threshold $m(k)$ does not exist in the asserted generality.

356349.title: The conjecture on subgroup perfect codes in connected Cayley sum graphs of symmetric groups
356349.statement: Let $n\geq 3$, and let a Cayley sum graph of the symmetric group $S_n$ be connected. A subgroup perfect code is a subgroup of $S_n$ that is a perfect code in this graph. **Subgroup perfect-code conjecture.** Every connected Cayley sum graph of $S_n$ has no subgroup perfect code. This conjecture asserts a generalization of the preceding result for $n=3,4$ or $5$; its status for all $n\geq 3$ is not established in the supplied text.

356462.title: Bašić et al.'s divisible-by-four degree conjecture for circulant nut graphs
356462.statement: Let $n$ be the order of a circulant graph, and let $\mathrm{Circ}(n,S)$ denote the circulant graph with generator set $S$. A **nut graph** is a non-trivial graph whose adjacency matrix has nullity one and whose non-zero null-space vectors have no zero elements. **Bašić et al.'s conjecture.** For every $d$ with $d\equiv 0\pmod 4$, and for every even $n$ with $n\geq d+4$, there exists a circulant nut graph $\mathrm{Circ}(n,\{a_1,a_2,a_3,\ldots,a_{d/2}\})$ of degree $d$. This is an existence conjecture for circulant nut graphs of every degree divisible by four; the supplied text gives no resolution status.

356476.title: Quadruple equidistribution conjecture for ascent-sequence statistics
356476.statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}_n$ be the set of ascent sequences of length $n$, and let $\mathsf{asc}$, $\mathsf{rep}$, $\mathsf{zero}$ and $\mathsf{max}$ denote their ascent-sequence statistics.

**Quadruple equidistribution conjecture.** For every $n\geq1$,

$$
\sum_{s\in\mathcal{A}_n}u^{\mathsf{asc}(s)}x^{\mathsf{rep}(s)}z^{\mathsf{zero}(s)}q^{\mathsf{max}(s)}=\sum_{s\in\mathcal{A}_n}u^{\mathsf{rep}(s)}x^{\mathsf{asc}(s)}z^{\mathsf{max}(s)}q^{\mathsf{zero}(s)}.
$$

Equivalently, the statistic quadruples $(\mathsf{asc},\mathsf{rep},\mathsf{zero},\mathsf{max})$ and $(\mathsf{rep},\mathsf{asc},\mathsf{max},\mathsf{zero})$ are equidistributed on ascent sequences. The source states that this conjecture is affirmed in the paper, so it is no longer open.

356718.title: Non-partition-regularity of the four-term pattern over bounded-degree polynomial semirings
356718.statement:
For $d\geq 1$, let $P_d$ be the set of polynomials in countably many variables with nonnegative integer coefficients, constant term, and degree at most $d$ in each variable. A finite pattern is **partition regular** over $P_d$ if every finite coloring of $P_d$ contains a monochromatic realization of the pattern. **Bounded-degree obstruction conjecture.** If $1\leq d<\infty$, then

$$
\{x,y,x+y,xy\}
$$

is not partition regular over $P_d$. The conjecture is known for $d=1$, using the two-coloring that colors reducible polynomials red and irreducible polynomials blue; whether the pattern is non-partition-regular over every finite-degree $P_d$ remains open.

356748.title: Classification conjecture for perfect restricted s-bases
356748.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, and let $m\geq2$ and $s\geq2$ be integers. A **perfect restricted $s$-basis** of size $m$ is a subset whose restricted sums of at most $s$ elements represent every element of $G$ uniquely. **Perfect restricted basis classification conjecture.** Such a basis exists if and only if $G$ has order $2^m$, or $G$ is isomorphic to one of

$$
\mathbb Z_{2^{s+1}-1},\quad \mathbb Z_2^{2s},\quad \mathbb Z^{2s-2}\times\mathbb Z_4.
$$

The paper gives examples in each listed family and a complete classification only for restricted $2$-bases; the asserted classification for all $m,s\geq2$ remains open.

356749.title: Classification conjecture for perfect spanning sets
356749.statement: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, and let $A$ be a perfect spanning set of size $m$ and radius $s$, meaning that every element of $G$ has a unique representation as a signed sum of at most $s$ elements of $A$. **Perfect spanning-set classification conjecture.** The only instances of perfect spanning sets are the three cases described in the source: $s=1$, arbitrary $m$; $m=1$, arbitrary $s$; or $m=2$, arbitrary $s$. In particular, one must have $s=1$ or $m\in\{1,2\}$. The source lists constructions for these three cases and conjectures that no others exist; the general classification remains open.

356922.title: Weak cordiality conjecture for trees and abelian groups
356922.statement: A family of graphs is **weakly $A$-cordial** if all but finitely many of its elements are $A$-cordial, where $A$ is an abelian group. **Weak cordiality conjecture.** For any abelian group $A$, the set of trees is weakly $A$-cordial. The result is known for $A=\mathbb{Z}_2^2$, since all trees except $P_4$ and $P_5$ are $\mathbb{Z}_2^2$-cordial. The conjecture remains open for arbitrary abelian groups.

356961.title: Hajebi's conjecture on subquadratic clique covers of K_{t,t}-free graphs
356961.statement:
Let $t\ge 1$ be an integer. A graph is **$K_{t,t}$-free** if it has no induced copy of the complete bipartite graph $K_{t,t}$, and a clique cover is a collection of cliques covering every edge.

**Hajebi's conjecture.** For every integer $t\ge 1$, there exists $\varepsilon>0$ such that every $K_{t,t}$-free graph $G$ has a clique cover of size

$$
O\left(|G|^{2-\varepsilon}\right).
$$

The conjecture is attributed to Sepehr Hajebi, who proposed it at a conference in Lyon. The paper proves a related bound with $\varepsilon=1/(2t)$, so the proposed statement is solved by the result described in the source.

357072.title: The eight-vertex bound for forbidden GaTEx subgraphs
357072.statement:
Let $\mathfrak{F}_{\mathrm{GT}}$ be the set of forbidden subgraphs of GaTEx graphs, and let $F\in\mathfrak{F}_{\mathrm{GT}}$. The preceding discussion shows that every such forbidden subgraph has at least five vertices.

**Eight-vertex bound.** For all $F\in\mathfrak{F}_{\mathrm{GT}}$, we have

$$
5\leq |V(F)|\leq 8.
$$

The lower bound follows from the fact that forbidden subgraphs must be primitive and cannot be pseudo-cographs, while the upper bound is motivated by the possibility of two vertex-disjoint induced $P_4$s. The claim is presented as a conjectural bound and no resolution is supplied here.

357849.title: Super vertex total local antimagic labeling existence conjecture
357849.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple undirected graph without isolated vertices. A **super vertex total local antimagic labeling** is a bijection $f:V\cup E\to\{1,2,\dots,|V|+|E|\}$ satisfying $w(u)\ne w(v)$ for every edge $uv\in E$, where

$$
w(v)=\sum_{x\in NT(v)}f(x),\qquad NT(v)=N(v)\cup\{uv:uv\in E\},
$$

and additionally $f(V)=\{1,2,\dots,|V|\}$. **The super vertex total local antimagic labeling conjecture.** Every graph without isolated vertices admits a super vertex total local antimagic labeling. The paper presents this as an existence problem for a broad class of graph labelings; no resolution is supplied here.

365571.title: Cichacz's 4-ZSPP conjecture for Abelian groups with more than one involution
365571.statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a finite Abelian group, and let $I(\Gamma)$ denote its set of involutions. A finite Abelian group has **4-ZSPP** if every integer partition of $|\Gamma|-1$ whose parts are all at least $4$ can be realized by a partition of $\Gamma^*=\Gamma\setminus\{0\}$ into zero-sum subsets of the corresponding sizes. **Cichacz's 4-ZSPP conjecture.** If $|I(\Gamma)|>1$, then $\Gamma$ has $3$-ZSPP. The surrounding text records later results proving the stronger assertion that every such group has $4$-ZSPP, so the stated conjecture is solved.

381874.title: Bang-Jensen et al.'s NP-completeness conjecture for bounded inversion number
381874.statement:
For a digraph $D$, let $\operatorname{inv}(D)$ be its inversion number, and let $k$ be a fixed positive integer.

**Bang-Jensen et al.'s complexity conjecture.** Deciding whether a given digraph $D$ has inversion number at most $k$ is NP-complete for any fixed positive integer $k$.

The paper notes that the case $k=1$ is already known to be NP-complete and that the dijoin conjecture would imply the asserted result for every fixed $k$. The source does not state a resolution.

381950.title: A vertex whose deletion decreases inversion number by at most one
381950.statement:
Let $D$ be a digraph with at least one vertex. For $v\in V(D)$, write $D-\{v\}$ for the digraph obtained by deleting $v$ and all incident edges.

**Vertex-deletion conjecture.** There exists $v\in V(D)$ such that

$$
\operatorname{inv}(D-\{v\})\geq\operatorname{inv}(D)-1.
$$

Equivalently, the general bound $\operatorname{inv}(D)\leq\operatorname{inv}(D-\{v\})+2$ cannot be tight for every vertex of the same digraph. The supplied text gives no resolution.

381984.title: Axiom for the small quasi-kernel conjecture
381984.statement: Let $D$ be a non-empty digraph. For a vertex $u\in V(D)$, let $d^+(u)$ denote its out-degree, let $N^+[u]$ denote its closed out-neighborhood, and call a vertex a source if it has in-degree zero. **Axiom for the small quasi-kernel conjecture.** There exists a vertex $u\in V(D)$ such that $d^+(u)>0$ and $D-N^+[u]$ has at most $d^+(u)$ sources not present in $D$. If this axiom holds for every directed graph, the paper's preceding argument proves the small quasi-kernel conjecture, namely that every source-free directed graph has a quasi-kernel of size at most half its vertices.

382041.title: Ivančo's supermagic labeling conjecture for Cartesian products of cycles
382041.statement: Let $C_n$ and $C_m$ be cycles with $n,m\geq 3$. A **supermagic labeling** of a graph with $q$ edges is a bijection from its edge set to $\{1,2,\dots,q\}$ such that the sums of the labels on edges incident with each vertex are equal. **Ivančo's conjecture.** The Cartesian product $C_n\Box C_m$ has a supermagic labeling for every $n,m\geq 3$. The conjecture extends the known cases of equal cycle lengths and of products of two even cycles; its general status is not specified in the source.
